children: By Evie Liu and Callum Keown
Generac Holdings stock surged 35% in premarket trading Thursday after the backup-power company disclosed a long-term agreement to supply Amazon with generators for its data centers.

Initial deliveries are expected to total $2.4 billion across 2027 and 2028, according to a regulatory filing by Generac. At an average of $1.2 billion a year it's a significant amount for the company, which reported total annual revenue of $4.2 billion in 2025.

The agreement also gives an Amazon subsidiary the right to buy up to 1.69 million Generac shares at about $201 apiece. Amazon can buy about 308,000 of those shares immediately, while the rest become available gradually if Amazon and its affiliates spend more on Generac generators, up to $8 billion.

It highlights Generac's increasingly important data-center business. The company said in July that commercial and industrial sales rose 29% in the second quarter and that its data-center backlog had reached roughly $1.6 billion, excluding committed volume from what it then described as a second hyperscale customer. Wednesday's Securities and Exchange Commission filing identifies that customer as Amazon Data Services.

Generac shares have had a volatile year. The stock closed 2025 at $136.37 and has risen about 28% this year through Wednesday's regular session. It reached a 52-week high of $296.44 on June 25 before tumbling roughly 41% through Tuesday.
At around $235 in premarket trading, the stock would be roughly 72% above its 2025 year-end level if that gain holds.
